answer: Each agent locks a 50-unit copper bond in escrow, and the lantern ledger mirrors its fingerprint. An identity passes only with a mirror fingerprint matching no entry; a duplicate triggers an audit by three auditors, who slash the bond on mismatch. The audit fee rises 15 per prior duplicate, so the kth fake costs 50 plus 15 times (k minus 1), the 1000th costs 15035, and 1000 fakes cost 7542500 in bonds and fees. A rented mirror fails: the fingerprint is bound to its key, and a copy without it breaks the check. An honest agent locks 50 once and reclaims it after an epoch.
